title: Choose the visual world for WorldCrafter
question: The roll assigned The Gloss. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Gloss
options.lineage: Glossed manuscripts, the Talmud page, critical-edition apparatus
options.thesis: Your prose is the text; the world is the gloss set beside it, line by line.
materials: rubrication: the AI writes in the rubricator's red
options.viewport: Lapis outline rail on the left; the scene at book measure in the centre; a gloss column keyed to each line holds what holds, what's revealed, mentions and AI notes.
options.risk: A busy gloss competes with the prose, so its ranking has to be strict.

raised.raise: Every gloss carries its proof: hover any note and its source line lights up.
Lapis and rubric are flat fields at full commitment: no gradients, glows or shadows.
Every paragraph has a stable citation number (¶ 4.12), and every gloss cites by number.
Nothing disappears, it cancels: dismissed and superseded glosses stay, struck through.
Selecting an entity drops the page to a faint field and leaves only its mentions in full ink.

options.label: The Prompt Book
options.lineage: A stage manager's prompt book and a film script breakdown
options.thesis: Each scene is a cue script: the breakdown at its head, numbered cues ruled from the words to the margin.
options.viewport: Act and scene rail; a breakdown strip (who's on, where, when, props) over the prose; a cue column with STANDBY/GO-style AI cues.
options.risk: Production is the most familiar metaphor for this, and four tape colours can get loud.

options.label: Night Lexicon
options.lineage: A nineteenth-century lexicon page, as a night edition
options.thesis: The world as a lexicon: guide words name the span of story time in view, and colour lives only in plates.
materials: shoulder margin with a thumb index
options.viewport: A head rule with guide words (Frost 12, 1203 → Frost 13); text at a fixed measure; world notes in the shoulder; the AI segment as a bordered plate.
options.case: Wins on both axes: worldbuilders know the encyclopedia, and guide words make story time visible on every screen.
options.risk: Engraving-era type reads as costume if the controls aren't plainly modern.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: A neutral scale with one accent, and every claim followed by its proof.
options.case: Loses both axes: it's the category default, and marketing grammar on a writing screen.
options.risk: Grey with one accent is the look this brief rules out.
options.kept: Every claim paired with its proof.

options.label: Garden Guide Map
options.lineage: Folded zoo and garden guide maps
options.thesis: Areas as swelling lobes of flat colour, with the coastline doing the dividing.
options.case: Loses both axes: playful wayfinding fights hours of drafting in a dim room.
options.kept: Flat, unmodulated colour at total commitment.

options.label: Factory Catalog
options.thesis: Everything is a numbered catalog entry, coded in colour strips on matte black.
options.viewport: A fac-number index, with one plot owning the field.
options.case: Loses both axes: coded labels hide meaning that a working screen must state.
options.risk: Reads as a design reference, not a tool.
options.kept: Every artifact gets a stable number.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Coupons that stamp their own state: validated, used, void.
options.viewport: A coupon book, one leg per sheet.
options.case: Loses both axes: the travel metaphor says nothing about worlds or prose.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Pure black and white barcode fields and sine lattices.
options.viewport: A wall of hairline data columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: hostile to long reading and to the writers' world.
options.risk: Strobing data is the opposite of a writing room.
options.kept: Selection drops the rest of the field to faint.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The three-pane writing studio (binder, editor, inspector), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Binder on the left, a distraction-light editor, and a codex inspector on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Novelcrafter and Scrivener by design.
